title: Registry-based randomized trial to determine the role of Oxygen in acute Pulmonary Embolism
official: Registry-based randomized trial to determine the role of Oxygen in acute Pulmonary Embolism
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of supplemental oxygen in patients with intermediate-risk acute pulmonary embolism at day 30.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Pulmonary embolism confirmed by multidetector computed tomographic pulmonary angiography
2. Right ventricular enlargement confirmed by computed tomography (transverse view) or echocardiography (apical or subcostal four chamber) where the right ventricle/left ventricle ratio is >1.0
Exclusion criteria:
1. Age less than 18 years
2. Participating in any other investigational drug or device study
3. Life expectancy <90 days at the discretion of the enrolling clinician
4. Oxygen saturation of less than 90% on pulse oximetry at the time of diagnosis
5. Technically inadequate basal computed tomography or echocardiography that prohibits the measurement of the right and left ventricle dimensions
6. Use of chronic oxygen therapy
7. Known hypercapnia (pCO2 >50 mmHg on arterial blood gases) at the time of diagnosis
8. Contraindication to anticoagulant therapy according to the physician judgement
9. Time elapsed since index diagnosis of pulmonary embolism symptom >10 days
10. Hemodynamic collapse at the time of PE diagnosis, defined as: need for cardiopulmonary resuscitation; or systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg for at least 15 min, or drop of systolic blood pressure by at least 40 mmHg for at least 15 min with signs of end organ hypoperfusion (cold extremities or low urinary output <30 mL/h or mental confusion); or need for catecholamine administration to maintain adequate organ perfusion and a systolic blood pressure of >90 mmHg
11. Inability to use mask or nasal prongs
